resources.string: 1. Open Settings and grant %1$s the overlay permission. This is for displaying an overlay over other apps.
2. Grant %1$s the notification permission (optional). Tapping on the notification will close the overlay and return you to this app.
3. For touch controls, enable "Middor Touch" in Android Accessibility settings. Skip this for view-only mirroring.
4. On the main screen, tap on the "%1$s" button.
5. Ensure that "Single App" is selected, then tap Start. Avoid the "Entire Screen" option, as this will also capture the overlay.
6. Select the application you want to mirror. This will launch the application, create the overlay and post a notification.
7. To exit, tap on the red Close (×) icon in the configured corner of the overlay (top right by default). Alternatively, you can pull down on your status bar and tap the notification.

1. The opaque mirror blocks direct touches to the hidden app. With touch controls enabled, taps, swipes, and multitouch gestures replay after finger-up, not in real time. A new gesture can interrupt replay. Touch feedback (off by default), tap duration, and the close-button corner are adjustable in Settings. Restart the mirror after changing settings.
2. Remove System Bars uses bar sizes measured at startup. Restart the mirror after rotating your device to update cropping.
